inputs.label: Application repository
inputs.what: The one GitHub OWNER/REPO whose account access and four workflow metadata records you want to observe.
inputs.why: This application repository is separate from the toolkit repository used by local workflow templates. No Git remote or project file is consulted.
inputs.where: Use the owner and repository name shown on your application's GitHub repository page. Do not paste a URL or a credential.
inputs.format: Exactly OWNER/REPO, at most 140 ASCII bytes; the existing core repository grammar applies. No branch, URL, host override or trailing slash.
inputs.failure: Invalid input is refused. A missing or inaccessible repository is not proof that it does not exist. Changing the target retires the original session; no automatic reconnection occurs.

inputs.label: Advanced session-only user token
inputs.what: When native entry is available, explicitly supply a user token in the gated password field to check your GitHub account and application repository. This app retains it for the native session only.
inputs.why: This independent, explicitly consented option does not require a GitHub CLI login or change its saved configuration/default account. It uses no GitHub App registration and is not a credential asset or persistent secret.
inputs.where: GitHub Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Fine-grained tokens. Select only the application repository and minimal Metadata/Actions read permissions. A token does not grant new repository access; organization approval may still be required. Never paste the token into a repository field, chat, config or file.
inputs.format: When native entry is available: nonempty printable ASCII without whitespace, at most 4096 bytes, entered only into the gated password field. No trimming, prefix-based trust, file import or plaintext persistence.
inputs.failure: Unqualified runtime, unavailable help or missing native ownership disables entry before collection. Unauthorized requires explicit new authentication after settlement. Forbidden can reflect token, organization or SSO policy; do not automatically escalate permissions.

guidance.label: Account observation is not release readiness
guidance.what: An authenticated account observation says which GitHub account answered the supplied read. Repository access is a separate fact.
guidance.why: Account login, local Apply and workflow listing do not authorize release, dispatch or remote setup. Broad powers of a supplied token would not be exercised here.
guidance.where: Use the selected GitHub CLI account or the separate session-only token field. For user-managed CLI sign-in, see https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_auth_login; it may change CLI configuration/default account and fall back to plaintext token storage. Browser/device sign-in inside this app remains unavailable and needs its own registered provider configuration and native transport.
guidance.format: One original native document/session, one explicit application repository and one original observation at a time. No automatic gh sign-in, account switch, environment token, credential helper or browser fallback.
guidance.failure: Unqualified, runtime-unavailable, publisher-unconfigured and not-connected are distinct from failed authentication. Busy blocks new Connect/Refresh, never retained Status or immediate exact-session Disconnect.

guidance.label: Reported roles are not effective grants
guidance.what: Pull, push and admin are reported repository-role observations: allowed, denied or unknown.
guidance.why: These flags do not prove effective token permissions, organization approval, environment access or authorization of a future mutation.
guidance.where: Review the selected repository and GitHub token settings manually. The existing core credential/environment checklist remains unknown/manual and is not reimplemented here.
guidance.format: Use only Metadata/Actions read access for this proposed route. No secret, variable, protection, runner or repository Actions settings are queried.
guidance.failure: 401 means unauthorized; 403 is forbidden, possibly organization/SSO policy; 404 means not-found-or-inaccessible. None is converted into a verified absence or an automatic request for wider scope.

guidance.label: Session-only lifetime and original settlement
guidance.what: This app retains its connection credential only in private native session memory, never in public status, draft, history, logs or a credential asset.
guidance.why: This app does not persist connection tokens or fall back to plaintext storage. User-managed GitHub CLI login stores credentials separately and may fall back to plaintext if secure storage fails.
guidance.where: Use Disconnect to retire local admission. Project/target/document changes, expiry and shutdown also require the native owner to stop its original consumers.
guidance.format: Proposed ceiling: 60 minutes from acceptance, shortened by known expiry. Status reads, refreshes and navigation do not renew it. Display timestamps are not deadline authority.
guidance.failure: Expired or cancelled facts are stale. Cleanup-unknown blocks further requests and cannot be cleared by late success. Dropping a Promise, disposing a view or requesting Disconnect is not proof of native settlement or memory erasure.

guidance.label: Bind the original immutable identities
guidance.what: Account, repository and remote workflow IDs are canonical positive decimal strings, not lossy JavaScript numbers.
guidance.why: A renamed, replaced or recreated target must not silently inherit the original observation or credential admission.
guidance.where: The future original owner retains account/repository IDs and brackets repository identity. The pure core projector only checks supplied data; it cannot certify the transport or custody.
guidance.format: At most five fixed HTTPS GETs, two 100-workflow pages, 256 KiB per body and 1 MiB combined, with no redirect/retry or returned-URL following. No network transport is activated by this increment.
guidance.failure: Target-changed refuses new identity adoption. Network-unavailable, TLS-failed, response-invalid and response-limit are fixed local failures, never raw response text or a suggestion to disable TLS.

guidance.label: Workflow metadata is not local-file verification
guidance.what: The four core-owned workflow IDs may be listed, not-listed or unknown, with active, disabled or unknown remote state.
guidance.why: Not-listed means only not returned by a complete bounded Actions listing. It says nothing about Git file absence, YAML compatibility, approvals or release readiness.
guidance.where: Compare this section with Local workflow files without merging their claims. Repository Actions settings/policy, environments, secrets, variables, protections and runners remain unobserved.
guidance.format: Exactly four rows in the existing core roster order. Incomplete coverage cannot report not-listed. Duplicate/changing listings become limited/unknown, not a complete snapshot.
guidance.failure: Rate-limited has no automatic retry. After a lost reply, inspect original Status rather than repeating Connect/Refresh. A later explicit read requires actual original settlement and native cooldown admission.

guidance.label: Remote setup remains unavailable
guidance.what: G1 is read-only: it neither edits remote repositories nor dispatches workflows. Local workflow Apply is a separate transaction and never means pushed.
guidance.why: Remote mutation requires its own plan, exact immutable target, fresh preconditions, confirmation, original one-use owner and reconciliation. Authentication does not supply those gates.
guidance.where: Keep Local workflow files, GitHub connection/observations and Remote setup visually separate. Existing protected-environment and Store guards remain unchanged.
guidance.format: Remote mutation and dispatch remain false; template compatibility and release readiness remain unknown. No secret values, workflow content, logs or arbitrary URLs are requested or displayed.
guidance.failure: There is no force, retry-write, latest-run adoption or secret-readback fallback. Ambiguous future writes must reconcile their original operation, not repeat it.

guidance.label: Local Disconnect is not remote revocation
guidance.what: Disconnect requests local retirement and cancellation of the exact original session, even while an observation is busy.
guidance.why: Remote grants remain controlled by GitHub. Starting a new login does not revoke an older token or grant.
guidance.where: For manual revocation, use GitHub Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens, or the relevant authorized GitHub App settings. No general browser opener is added here.
guidance.format: Status remains readable without renewing lifetime. Release of private material follows actual native settlement; unknown cleanup retains ownership.
guidance.failure: Never assume successful cancellation or erasure from a click, closed view or lost reply. Keep cleanup-unknown visible and do not start another connection to repair it.
